speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Oh, first it was Grenada
and then Lebanon.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Yeah, I know what you mean.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Seems like every time I start to get close
to a girl, she gets shipped out.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Well, maybe this next case
will cheer him up.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Let me guess. This guy was caught
peeping into their dressing room.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
He's the victim, Your Honor.
The ladies are the defendants.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Do you mean to tell me these sweet,
innocent-looking young women...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Beat the snot out of this man. Right.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, my clients
were lured to New York...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...under the guise of a legitimate
beauty contest.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It turned out that Mr. Harris here did not
have the prize money he claimed to have.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
The girls found out during the competition
and they responded.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, according to witnesses,
Miss Congeniality led the attack...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
The one in the polka suit over there
tried to twist my lips off.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: That will be enough of that language.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I mean the bickering, not the Swedish.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, it's not only Swedish,
but Italian...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Weren't there any interpreters
at the pageant?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
All his budget allowed for was
one videotape machine...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Hey, come on. This is for cable TV.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I ain't got bucks to throw around
like those network productions.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I could do a whole show...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...for what one of those
Barbara Mandrell outfits go for.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...but evidently your profit comes
at some expense to others.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...the fact is that this man is not the one
who is on trial here...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...although the people will agree his actions
were scum-like in nature.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
He twisted these girls' innocent
hopes and dreams into...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, I would like
a continuance of this case...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...until interpreters can be found
and these ladies are provided for.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Your Honor, being a speaker of English...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...I can make my statement now
if it would help.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I like to help. That's why
I'm majoring in speech therapy.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It's a way to help those less
fortunate than ourselves...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...learn the ability to communicate
and function as productive human beings...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I've got some paper bags in the office
if you feel the need to:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I just love our system of justice,
Your Honor.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
That system works for me,
and by golly, I'll work for it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Barton Jewelry Store was
the offended establishment, Your Honor.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Ms. Brandon, do you have anything to say?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You're even better-looking
than I imagined.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I'll get those paper bags now.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...his hair was dark
like his Uncle Otto.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Who would think it would have
lightened up so much?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Yes. Goes nicely with the robe.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Then I take it we have met?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'm afraid you have the advantage,
Miss Brandon. I just don't remember you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
The last time I saw you,
you were only 5.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ... The Merv Griffin Show last night?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - He had this talking bird on...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Could she really be your mother?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
My mom walked out on me
when I was 5.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Dad never talked about her and frankly, after
he died, I never thought much about her.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Anyway, the bird says to Merv...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You mean, you never thought
about where your mother was...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...what she was doing, whether she was
dead or alive?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Honestly, I never thought about it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I mean, when I was
a kid growing up...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...Mother's Day didn't mean anything more
to me than Groundhog's Day.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Never had one of those, either.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor, can I use
some of the petty cash...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...to buy food for those bathing beauties?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Sure. How are they getting along?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Well, as far as I can tell...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I just hope they know that at 30...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Bull. You know, like the animal?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: No, no, no. Not a cow.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - You've got to talk to her. That's a given.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I admit that it's possible
that she's not your mother...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It would look better if they
were lighted, wouldn't it?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I understand you're diverting yourself.
I mean, it's very hard to handle...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Why don't I make you a nice cup of tea...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - I've got your favorite, cherry Kool-Aid!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Maybe you're right. I mean, some woman
waltzes in here with strange claims.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I mean, that's no reason for us to jump
to any definite conclusions.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Your Honor? My client would like to have
a few minutes with you, if possible.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Sure. Come on in. The more the merrier.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Well, if you'll all excuse me...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I know I haven't been here for very long,
and sometimes I...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Well, sometimes I don't know what the hell
you're talking about.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'd like to pass on some advice
that my Uncle Lionel used to give me:

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - He sounds like a wise man.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: We have no idea why he killed himself.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - No, I don't think you do.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: When I had you, I was young.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I couldn't handle it.
I wasn't ready for it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - What I'm trying to say is...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Anybody who would leave their child
can't be emotionally well, can she?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Miss Brandon, you're upset,
and maybe you're a little mixed-up.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
All you've done is broken a window.
It's not that serious.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
When you were little,
you had a little red wagon.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Miss Brandon, lots of little boys
had little red wagons.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
And you used to take your dog Oliver
for rides in it.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Yeah. In fact, there was this bird on The Merv Griffin Show...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Oh, I don't want anything, Harry.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I don't want anything from you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I just came here to tell you...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Well, I've taken up enough of your time.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Uncle Otto. How many thumbs
did he have?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: And it's shaped like a little star.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I bet Harry could just die!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I mean, what an embarrassing place
for a man to have a birthmark.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Now, just give this piece of paper
to the cabby.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: And tell him to take you there.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I assure you there will be
no funny business...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Now, this is just an offer to help you...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Perhaps if we think of it
merely as a testimony...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Story here about a man who ate
nothing but seaweed for three years.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Yeah. You got any chocolate cigarettes?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - So how did it go with your...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Well, she seems to know a lot about me.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I've got this blurry 30-year-old photograph.
Could be her.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Yeah. Then I made a few phone calls,
and some things do fit.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: So you think it's a possibility?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
There are more things
in heaven and earth...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Can I show you something
in a bubble-gum cigar?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'm Barbara, but my friends
call me Buffy.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - Well, then let's give you one.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I mean, I have to be
running along myself...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Selma, don't you have to go too?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Oh, Liz told me about the store owner...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...dropping the charges
if I offer to pay for the window.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: It was very nice to see you, Harry.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Maybe... Maybe you wanna hang around
for a while and watch the session.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
And then afterwards, we could go out
and have a drink or some coffee...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Oh, yeah, sure. I'd like that.
I love to talk.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Having listened to the testimony
and read the statements...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...the court finds the defendants
not guilty.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Oh, what a surprise! I wasn't expecting it. I
don't have a prepared statement or anything!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
We've made provisions for all the women
through their consulates...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Nobody was there when we called,
but they will be and she'll be taken there.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: We won't have to use these.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Of course, you all don't have to go
to your consulates if you don't want to.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Would you tell her that?
No, go ahead. Tell her that.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Lives have been laid down so that you have
the right to assemble anywhere you wish!

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Excuse me. Who do I see about
finding somebody who was arrested?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Do you know where I can find
Mrs. Eleanor Brandon?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Thank God! Ma, what are you doing here?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
They told me you were under arrest
for breaking a window.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: It's all straightened out. Don't worry.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Look, I am sorry if she has caused
you any trouble.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: No trouble. No trouble at all.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Actually, she has been doing a lot of...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...weird things for the last couple of years,
and, well...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...I think we're gonna have to seriously
consider putting her in a home...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
No, you're not, Ma.
You're in an adult apartment complex.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: People her own age, communal meals...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: It is not a jail, Ma.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: So how come I'm not allowed visitors?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - So how come I never see you there?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Mom, can we not
go into this now, please?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - I've got a business to run.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Oh, well, listen, Your Honor, I apologize.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I didn't know she was bothering you.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
That's a lonely lady there,
Mr. Brandon.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - No, I think it's hers you ought to beg.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I don't understand a word you're saying.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You know, I don't like your tone
in my courtroom, Mr. Brandon.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'm going to sentence you
for contempt of court.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Sentence me for contempt of court?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
It is the sentence of this court that
you be held in contempt and jailed...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...until such time as you choose to...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...take advantage of the fact
that you got a mother.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: And if you can't see that now...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...then no amount of time in jail is
gonna help you see it any more clearly.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
The court withdraws
the contempt charge.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
You have a lot of pets,
don't you, Eleanor?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
The man at the pet store told me
I overfed them, though.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I thought floating was just
their way of resting.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Come on, Ma. I'll take you back.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Fish can't talk to you, Leonard.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Oh, thank you very much, sir.
I'll make a note of that.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
She misses you so much
that she invented another son.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: A judge? You harassed a judge?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I can't believe that you would do that.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Can you believe that she would do that?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Maybe I ought to be put away.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: - How did you know so much about me?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...about how you grew up
without a mother...

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: ...and then I did a little more research.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: And then you decided to adopt me, huh?

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Lucky guess. I almost said three.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
...that maybe you'd get something
out of this too.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: I did. I really did, Eleanor.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
But don't ever do that to another
human being for the rest of your life.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
Come on, Ma.
Let's go get something to eat.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text:
I'm sorry, Leonard.
Eleanor and I have a date.

speaker: UNKNOWN
text: Mom always did like you best.
